$comment: Cross-language contract for the duplicate-name key.
Two implementations must agree exactly, in two languages, or the import
guard and the pre-screen report disagree about what a duplicate is:
Same idea as pipeline/contract/coverage-contract.json: one file, asserted
from both sides, so neither can drift alone. Each case names the rule it
exists to hold. Add a case when you add a rule.

cases.why: a hyphen SEPARATES: it becomes a space
cases.name: Saint-Roch

cases.why: and the spaced spelling reduces to the same thing
cases.name: Saint Roch

cases.why: an apostrophe JOINS inside a word: it comes off with no space
cases.name: St Mary's

cases.why: the abbreviation point comes off too
cases.name: St. Mary's

cases.why: a trailing place qualifier is dropped at the first comma
cases.name: St Mary's Cathedral, Perth

cases.why: an en dash reads as a separator, not as nothing
cases.name: Liège–Bastogne–Liège

cases.why: so does a soft hyphen, which is invisible in an editor
cases.name: Liege­Bastogne

cases.why: so does a unicode minus sign
cases.name: Liege−Bastogne

cases.why: leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed
cases.name: Hôtel Koru

cases.why: an ampersand is punctuation, not a separator
cases.name: Water & food

cases.why: digits survive: they are part of the name
cases.name: 7 Rue des Marchés

cases.why: two genuinely different dedications stay different
cases.name: St Johns Cathedral

cases.why: a name that is only punctuation reduces to nothing, and callers must treat an empty key as no key
